issues.description: teleport_s parameter order is inconsistent between the problem statement and the provided code. The problem statement specifies teleport_s(circ, data_qubit, injection_qubit, p=0.0), but both template and solution define teleport_s(circ, injection_qubit, data_qubit, p=0.0). Students following the written spec will swap the qubits and build the wrong teleportation circuit (or fail tests expecting the documented API).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the teleport_s signature consistent across all artifacts. Prefer matching the problem statement by changing template and solution to: def teleport_s(circ: stim.Circuit, data_qubit: int, injection_qubit: int, p: float = 0.0) -> int, and update internal calls accordingly; alternatively, update the problem statement to reflect the existing (injection_qubit, data_qubit) order, but keep everything consistent.

issues.description: The inject docstring misdescribes the role of injection_qubit compared to the problem statement and the implemented behavior. The problem statement says injection_qubit is the resource ancilla that is measured (consumed) during injection, but the template docstring says it is "the ancilla qubit that will receive the data", which reverses the intended roles and can mislead students implementing the circuit.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template inject docstring to match the problem statement and solution behavior: injection_qubit is the prepared |Y> ancilla/resource qubit that is entangled with data_qubit and then measured; the function returns the index of that measurement.

issues.description: build_msd_circ return-value documentation is inconsistent between the problem statement and the template docstring. The problem statement says the second returned list must be the measurement indices for the destructive X-basis measurements of the 15 tetrahedral-code qubits (in qubit order), but the template docstring incorrectly describes it as "final X-basis measurements of the distilled state". The solution returns indices for MRX on the 15 code qubits, matching the problem statement.
issues.suggestedFix: Fix the template build_msd_circ docstring to state that the second returned list contains the measurement indices of the destructive X-basis measurements of the 15 tetrahedral-code qubits, ordered according to the code-qubit ordering.

issues.description: The template inject signature omits the type annotation for injection_qubit (defined as inject(circ, data_qubit: int, injection_qubit) -> int) while the rest of the API and the problem statement treat injection_qubit as an int qubit index. This is a minor but inconsistent type-hinting mismatch that can confuse students relying on annotations.
issues.suggestedFix: Add the missing type annotation in the template: def inject(circ: stim.Circuit, data_qubit: int, injection_qubit: int) -> int.
